speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your jaundice and dark urine, when did these symptoms first begin, and have you noticed any abdominal pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the painless jaundice, weight loss, and pale stools, I suspect a malignancy such as pancreatic cancer or cholangiocarcinoma. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal CT scan

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan was normal, I need to look closer at the biliary tree. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP demonstrates dilation of the common bile duct and intrahepatic bile ducts with a cutoff in the distal common bile duct. No discrete mass is visualized, but the stricture is suspicious for a periampullary or pancreatic head malignancy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP findings strongly suggest a distal common bile duct obstruction, likely from a small pancreatic head or ampullary tumor missed by the initial CT. I will proceed to visualize the biliary tree directly and obtain tissue for diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: ERCP with biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ERCP demonstrates a stricture in the distal common bile duct. Biopsy of the stricture reveals adenocarcinoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma, which explains your obstructive jaundice and weight loss. DIAGNOSIS READY: Adenocarcinoma of the distal common bile duct
